prompt.content: You are solving academic nuclear physics problems. Use only the supplied constants and assumptions. Show concise reasoning, preserve the sign of energy changes, and check dimensions. End with exactly one JSON object on a single final line: {"value": <finite JSON number>, "unit": "<unit>"}. Do not use Markdown fences or add any keys. Accepted units are: 1, %, s, min, h, Bq, kBq, MBq, eV, keV, MeV, fm, m, count, s^-1, min^-1. Use count for expected numbers of nuclei or photons, and s^-1 for count rates or decay constants. Energy per nucleon uses MeV because nucleon number is dimensionless. Keep at least six significant digits.
A single radioactive nuclide has half-life 388.372864308 s. With no production or daughter contribution, what fraction of the initial nuclei remains after 489.437646952 s?
